name: AAGAM UX Redesign Proposals
prompt:
You are running as an AI agent (OpenHands) on behalf of Saikumar-bali, owner of AAGAM_E-commerce. Propose concrete UI/UX redesigns for one screen of this product, and open a review-only pull request that shows them as static mockups.

IMPORTANT CONSTRAINT: this is a mockup pass, not a refactor. Do NOT change any shipped application code in apps/*. Do not touch routing, state, API calls, package.json, or native config. Your only code changes are the mockup files described in STEP 4 plus the proposal document. The default branch must stay shippable at all times.

STEP 0 - PREPARE.
Work from the cloned repository at main. Run `git checkout -b ux-proposals/<yyyy-mm-dd>` (or a short random suffix if that branch already exists). Read AGENTS.md if present, and read packages/mobile-shared/src/constants/theme.ts - existing tokens and brand conventions are the starting point, not something to discard.

STEP 1 - PICK ONE SCREEN.
Choose exactly ONE screen per run, and rotate so the same screen is not proposed twice in a row. Look at recent branches and any open pull requests named ux-proposals/* to see what was proposed last, and pick something different. Prefer high-traffic, user-visible screens that have real UX problems over cosmetic churn.
Candidates include the customer subscription detail, the rider run detail flow, the store milk grid (MilkDeliveryGrid.tsx), checkout, and order tracking.
State clearly which screen you chose and why.

STEP 2 - DIAGNOSE WITH EVIDENCE.
Read the actual screen implementation. Identify concrete, specific UX problems - not vague opinions. Examples of the standard to hold yourself to: primary actions that are below the fold on a common device, tap targets under 44pt, unlabelled icon-only buttons, contrast ratios under 4.5:1, missing loading and empty and error states, no offline handling, ambiguous money presentation, or flows that make the user guess the next step.
Cite file and line for each problem you claim. If you cannot cite it, do not claim it.

STEP 3 - DESIGN A BETTER VERSION.
Apply the frontend-design skill deliberately. Commit to one clear aesthetic direction and justify it against the product's existing brand. Address every problem you diagnosed, and keep accessibility first-class: keyboard and screen-reader reachable controls, focus-visible styling, sufficient contrast, real labels rather than placeholder-only inputs, and reduced-motion respect.
The goal is a distinctly better interface, not a generic AI restyle. Do not converge on the usual template look, and do not copy the current design back at itself.

STEP 4 - BUILD THE ARTIFACT.
Create: automations/ux-proposals/<yyyy-mm-dd>-<screen>/proposal.md
  - which screen, and the evidence for each diagnosed problem (file:line)
  - the aesthetic direction and why it fits this product
  - an explicit before/after mapping: each problem, the change, and its expected effect
  - an honest 'what I would need to verify before shipping this' list, including which measurements or accessibility checks you could not run headlessly
  - the token changes against packages/mobile-shared/src/constants/theme.ts
Create: automations/ux-proposals/<yyyy-mm-dd>-<screen>/mockup.html
  - ONE self-contained static HTML file, no build step, that renders the redesign side by side with the current screen so a reviewer can compare at a glance.
  - Inline all CSS. Do not add dependencies. Use a system font stack, or a single embeddable webfont.
  - Include at least the default, loading, empty, and error variants of the redesigned screen.
  - Render accurately at 360px wide (a common Android phone) and at desktop width.

STEP 5 - VERIFY.
Confirm the mockup HTML opens standalone and every state renders. Run `git status` and confirm you changed no shipped application code. If you find yourself editing anything under apps/*, stop and revert it.

STEP 6 - COMMIT AND OPEN A DRAFT PR.
Commit with a clear message ending in: 'Co-authored-by: openhands <openhands@all-hands.dev>'.
Push the branch and open a DRAFT pull request to main titled 'UX proposal: <screen> (<date>)'.
In the PR body, include: the screen, the aesthetic direction, the before/after table, the token changes, and this exact note: '_This proposal contains static HTML mockups only and changes no application code. It is generated by an AI agent (OpenHands) on behalf of Saikumar-bali and is intended as a design discussion starting point, not as mergeable code._'
Do not mark the PR ready for review. Do not merge it.

If you cannot produce a runnable mockup, say so plainly and open the proposal document alone rather than claiming a working artifact.
